context: Kenji shows Sho-young a sports event; cheering on a young athlete.
purpose: Mentor and child engaged in sports admiration.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 健司おじちゃん、この選手、すごい!
lines.style: Bright, open-mouthed wonder. Sharp intake of breath on the exclamation. Voice climbs on 「すごい」. Genuine awe without self-consciousness — the unfiltered enthusiasm of a perceptive child.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.en: Yeah — nice angle for filming that!
lines.style: Warm, conspiratorial approval. Soft Kansai cadence. Leans into the shared moment of noticing something good. Encouraging without making a big show of it.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: He must be really frustrated after losing.
lines.style: Quiet, considerate. Small voice — not stating the obvious loudly but naming what he notices. Gentle empathy, the kind that doesn't require reassurance back.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: うまく、立ち直るで、必ず。
lines.en: But he'll bounce back. I'm sure he will.
lines.style: Soft Kansai confidence. Not lecturing — more like a quiet promise. Warm, steady tone. The certainty of someone who's seen people recover before.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 舞台、こんな大きいんやな。
lines.en: The stage is really this big.
lines.style: Hushed discovery. Slight lift of wonder at the end. Processing something larger than expected. Quiet amazement at the scale, spoken almost to himself.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.en: Look at the audience reaction — it's incredible!
lines.style: Bright, animated Kansai warmth. Energy lifted. Pointing it out with genuine delight, inviting Sho to see what he's seeing. Unguarded enthusiasm.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: You can really feel how much it moves people.
lines.style: Soft, genuine reflection. Slight slowdown in pace — absorbing the moment rather than commenting on it. Warm, almost tender. The voice of someone who just understood something bigger.
